findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext drops every log written through it
findings.body: `FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, which is a new, unrelated instance. Code that now logs through `logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (for example `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` at logger_middleware.go:58) will never bump `InfoLogs.Calls` on the `TestLogger` a test injected. A test written against this fake would see zero calls and either fail for the wrong reason or end up asserting nothing. Returning `f` would keep the recorded logs visible to the test. `New` (line 18) already has the same pattern, so this is a judgement call. Still, `FromContext` is now the main logging path for the middleware, so it matters more here.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running before it
findings.body: `logRequest` no longer adds `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName` or `dsUID` itself. Those attributes only show up if `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` sits earlier in the chain, which it does today (pluginsintegration.go:160-161). If the middlewares are reordered, or `NewLoggerMiddleware` is used without the contextual one, the "Plugin Request Completed" egress log loses these fields with no error. The old InstrumentationMiddleware doc spelled out its ordering requirement, and this PR removed that comment (metrics_middleware.go:24-25). A short comment on `NewLoggerMiddleware`, or on the middleware list, would keep the dependency visible.

findings.title: No tests for the new contextual logger middleware or the refactored logger middleware
findings.body: `instrumentContext` moved here from metrics_middleware.go, and `LoggerMiddleware` now takes all its plugin/request attributes from the context. Neither change has a test. The clientmiddleware package has no `contextual_logger_middleware_test.go` or `logger_middleware_test.go`. One test that runs a request through ContextualLogger → Logger and checks that the emitted log contains `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsUID` and `uname` would cover the behaviour this PR claims to keep. Note that the `TestLogger` fake can't observe this today (see the fake.go finding).

findings.title: Test function still named after the old middleware
findings.body: The middleware was renamed to `MetricsMiddleware` and the test now calls `newMetricsMiddleware` (line 78), but the test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Renaming it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` would match the new name.

contracts.action: ContextualLoggerMiddleware inserted between MetricsMiddleware and LoggerMiddleware to attach plugin/request log attributes to ctx
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this PR, InstrumentationMiddleware.instrumentPluginRequest called instrumentContext right before fn(ctx), after pluginTarget succeeded
contracts.before_after: MetricsMiddleware still returns early with ErrPluginNotRegistered before calling next (metrics_middleware.go:105-108, 149-151). So the contextual middleware, which sits after it, only runs when the plugin exists, the same as before. instrumentContext is identical to the removed version and uses the same WithContextualAttributes. Stream methods pass ctx through unchanged, as they did before.
contracts.visible_effect: Loggers further down the chain that call FromContext (including LoggerMiddleware and plugin code) get endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname attributes. The traceID comes from the tracing log provider.
contracts.failure_mode: No async or failure path. instrumentContext is pure context wrapping.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of adding pluginId/endpoint/uname/ds/traceID params itself
contracts.equivalent_path: The old logRequest added these params explicitly, plus traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)
contracts.before_after: ConcreteLogger.FromContext collects the args from all registered providers: the logParamsContextKey provider registered in init, and the tracing provider that emits traceID using the same TraceIDFromContext(ctx,false) call. It then returns cl.New(args...). So the attributes match the old log, as long as ContextualLoggerMiddleware runs upstream.
contracts.visible_effect: The "Plugin Request Completed" egress log carries the same keys as before, possibly in a different order.
contracts.failure_mode: If ContextualLoggerMiddleware is not earlier in the chain, the plugin/ds/user attributes are dropped silently. Reported as a consider finding.

contracts.before_after: ConcreteLogger.FromContext returns either cl.New(args...), which is a *ConcreteLogger, or cl itself. So the type assertion always succeeds, and the d.New() fallback is unreachable today.
contracts.visible_effect: The plugin logger carries the contextual attributes.
contracts.failure_mode: The fallback d.New() returns a logger without the contextual attributes. This is harmless because that branch can't currently be reached.

summary: This PR is a refactor. It renames InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware, moves the contextual-logger setup into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware placed right after it, and has LoggerMiddleware take its plugin and request attributes, including traceID, from the context through a new plog.Logger.FromContext. I traced the path and the egress log keeps the same attributes. The new middleware runs only when the plugin exists, the same as before. The traceID still comes from the tracing log provider. The type assertion in the wrapper always succeeds. I found no bugs, only four consider-level findings: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so anything logged through it is invisible to tests. LoggerMiddleware now quietly depends on the order of the middleware chain. Neither the new middleware nor the refactored logger middleware has a test. The metrics test function still has its old name.
